answer: Each epoch, agents must answer a challenge word drawn from a randomness beacon, weaving it naturally into their output - today it might be sonnet, yesterday quill. Since the beacon reveals the word only moments before the epoch closes, an attacker cannot precompute template responses across thousands of fake identities. Each sybil needs a live reasoning model per identity per epoch, so cost scales linearly with fakes instead of amortizing, and the beacon signal makes stale prepared answer pools worthless.
